summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: almost every Hindi video gets hundreds of views there, while YouTube Shorts barely moves (most under 30 views). The best videos are Hindi explainers about a sensor that seems to 'see' or 'sense' something magically (PIR motion sensor, robot avoiding walls), and they earn the most shares and saves. Weak ones are generic or feature-style titles (smoke detector, ultrasonic, TV remote, touchscreen) that get views but almost no shares or saves.
winningPattern: Hindi (Hinglish) Instagram Reels about a familiar everyday or robot behavior framed as a mystery: 'X doesn't do Y, so how does it Z?' The title opens with a surprising claim or 'kaise' question, ends with 🤔, and names one sensor (PIR, IR). Robot/security/motion subjects beat abstract phone or display topics. Shares come from relatable 'robot avoids wall' style stories.
doMore: Lead with a contradiction hook ('Sensor aapko dekhta nahi!') and answer it within 3 seconds of the video
Pick subjects that feel like a robot or security behavior (obstacle avoidance, motion detection, line following)
Post Hindi Reels to Instagram first, since it gives about 10-100x more views than YouTube
End with a share-worthy line or a prompt like 'Doston ko bhejo jo sochte hain...' to lift shares and saves
Make a short series on one sensor family (PIR, IR) with the same title format, since those two topped the list
stopDoing: Near-duplicate topics like two smoke detector videos and two IR videos within days; combine or space them out
Cross-posting Hindi titles to YouTube Shorts expecting the same result; test an English title and hook there instead, since the English Arduino video got 160 views on YouTube
